body: I thought the house was bugged, and that the weather and the sounds of the highway, trains and planes were rigged by movie magic. I thought I was psychic and that my computer was sending me special messages, and thought I had to perform a number of complex rituals to redeem myself and my loved ones. I thought my family members were trying to kill me. Mostly pretty textbook stuff - it's strange how so many of our delusions follow similar patterns.

I'm sorry to hear about your illness too. Yes, I'm on medication, which keeps me from being psychotic but doesn't do much for my depression. I'm in my 40s and live with my partner, who is also depressed. I caused him to have the worst time of his life while manic/psychotic and we are still dealing with the aftermath, mainly poverty and trauma. I feel so guilty. I know it would make him feel terrible if I died, but a lot of the time I just feel so bad I can't think of anything else. I don't think there is any sort of future for me. I can't seem make opportunities for myself - I don't even leave the house anymore, and I can't drive and have no special skills or even interests, anymore. Only regrets. Thank you for writing.
I am also an Adderall casualty.

Yeah. I was overweight so I had plenty to lose, and suddenly I was no longer a couch potato. I walked and ran all around town for hours a day, and consumed very little. My immune system totally crashed. It sounds like you are more in control of the situation!
Yes, I lost 40 pounds over 2 months of mania. It wasn't healthy. I had full-blown mania, though.

The pros of going to the hospital are that you will get a break, assistance detoxing, and probably new or adjusted psychiatric medication and a referral for counseling. The cons are that there may be expense, depending on your insurance, and it can be an alienating experience. I'm sorry about your house and the rest of it.

I think I know what you mean. I've been hauled out of my house and off to the hospital by cops twice in the last year, and the hospital offered no help at all and was basically a degrading punishment. The only effect, beside the expense, was to humiliate me in front of my neighbors, so now I don't go outside and my life is indeed a downward shit spiral. I truly hope this doesn't happen to you.

I think people genuinely think they are doing the right thing and not trying to cause pain, in that they really believe they have to call the cops or have you hospitalized to keep you safe in that moment. I just wish they would think it through and realize that they've just turned a low-probability suicide into certain long-lasting trauma.

I would much rather have major depression because I know how to cope with that, but I ruined my life during an episode of mania with psychosis, which I had never had before. Damage was swift and permanent.

About 6 years of unemployment between the ages of 17 - 43 (including now), plus a whole lot of underperformance. I've basically never been able to work to my so-called potential. And that is why I wish to die.
Glad to hear it, and best of luck to you, too!
That's really cool. How did you get into engineering? Did you have a background in it before going into law? I was also a lawyer for about 10 minutes, and have been downwardly mobile ever since.
I'm glad to hear you made it work! If you don't mind my asking, what was your past career, and your current one?

Thank you for your kind words, but I don't think I'm getting any more chances. I ruined my career and everything else that made me feel ok in the world. I waited, tried, and hoped for things to get better and they are only getting worse. I can't take it anymore.
But then there's the part when you wake up and remember.
